speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why should one recite the supreme mantra of the glorious seat?
premises: Its purpose is enjoyment and liberation.
inference: Recitation of this mantra serves both enjoyment and liberation.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What knowledge is not superior to equal vision of Kaula?
premises: Kaula equal vision is denied as inferior.
inference: Neither veda-superior knowledge nor mere equal vision of Kaula is the final claim.
uncertainties: Whether kaulasamadarśanam is subject or predicate.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is this truth repeated three times without doubt?
inference: The statement is affirmed emphatically as certain truth.
uncertainties: Which referent each idaṃ picks out.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why can the speaker not describe it even in countless kalpas?
premises: Even kalpa-crores of hundreds do not suffice.
inference: The greatness exceeds any finite description.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What greatness of the mantra has been spoken to you?
premises: Thus some mantra greatness has been spoken.
It was spoken by me to you.
inference: A partial account of mantra greatness has been given.
uncertainties: Whether kiñcit modifies amount or quality.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What more does the goddess wish to hear after this?
premises: This has been spoken to you.
O goddess, what do you wish to hear again?
inference: The dialogue invites a further question from the goddess.
uncertainties: Whether te is dative or genitive.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the name of the third illumination?
premises: The narration of the supreme mantra is named.
inference: This section is titled the narration of the supreme mantra of the glorious seat.
uncertainties: Whether nāma is indeclinable or participle.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is the lord asked to speak the mantra king with nyāsa and meditation?
premises: O lord, with nyāsa, meditation, and so forth.
inference: The request includes ritual accompaniments to the mantra king.
uncertainties: Whether saha governs the instrumental phrase.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What arises merely by hearing it?
premises: By mere hearing of it, Śiva-form arises.
inference: Hearing alone produces the form of Śiva.
uncertainties: Whether tasya refers to mantra or lord.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why does the speaker declare this today out of affection?
premises: From your affection I speak today.
inference: Affection motivates the present disclosure.
uncertainties: Whether matprāṇavallabhe is vocative or instrumental.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What fruit does the supreme mantra give?
premises: The supreme mantra of the glorious seat gives fruit.
That fruit is enjoyment and liberation.
inference: The mantra bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
uncertainties: Whether bhukti and mukti are separate fruits or one compound fruit.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why does the mantra give direct fruit?
inference: Its nature as light-bliss and direct fruit-giving explains its efficacy.
uncertainties: Whether these are two separate reasons or one compound reason.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What does grace-making make praised quickly?
inference: The seat is praised quickly through grace-making.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What two sources justify the supreme mantra?
premises: supreme bliss generation is a source
supreme dharma indication is a source
inference: The supreme mantra is justified by supreme bliss generation and supreme dharma indication.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is it called the supreme mantra?
inference: Because of supremacy over all mantras, it is called the supreme mantra.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What should one do first in the morning?
inference: First one rises in the morning and contemplates guru and deity.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What purifications and rites should one perform?
inference: One should perform mouth cleansing, bathing, and sandhyā libation.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What follows after entering the worship place?
inference: After entering the worship place, one sits on the seat.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What salutations are made to the goddess?
premises: gaṇa and field protector are saluted
inference: The goddess is addressed with seat, gaṇa, and field-protector salutations.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Where are hand-limb purification and breath control done?
premises: own brahma aperture is the place
inference: Hand-limb purification and breath control are done in one's own brahma aperture.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What script is named ten-fold being?
premises: a ten-fold being-named script is named
it is an object of placement
inference: The tortoise-named script, called ten-fold being, is to be placed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Who is the deity here among all mantras?
premises: she is supreme lady of all mantras
inference: Here Gāyatrī is the deity, supreme lady of all mantras.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: By what seed are the six limbs made?
inference: O Pārvatī, the six limbs are made by the six-long root seed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Where should the image be placed after fingers?
premises: image is placed in five fingers
then it is placed in mouths
inference: Having placed the image in the five fingers, one should place it in the mouths.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: From which power should one begin and where should one end in this rite?
inference: The practitioner proceeds from ādhāraśakti through pīṭhamantra.
uncertainties: Exact ritual scope beyond these endpoints is not stated.
